assets.caption: Course roadmap. Seven stages connect foundational workflows to advanced specialist practice.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf teaching diagram created for this course; no external artwork used.

assets.purpose: Workflow lifecycle concept diagram
assets.alt_text: Six stages: event, scheduler, runner, result, outputs, and next stage.
assets.caption: Workflow lifecycle. A repository event triggers scheduling, runner execution, reporting, and optional artifact promotion.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf teaching diagram created for this course; no external artwork used.

assets.purpose: Job dependency graph concept diagram
assets.alt_text: A workflow trigger fans into lint and test jobs; both feed a build job, which then precedes a protected deployment.
assets.caption: Job dependency graph. Independent quality checks run in parallel; build waits for both; deployment follows the verified build.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf teaching diagram created for this course; no external artwork used.

assets.purpose: Artifact vs. dependency cache concept diagram
assets.alt_text: A side-by-side conceptual comparison of artifacts for run outputs and caches for rebuildable dependencies, with their security notes.
assets.caption: Artifact vs. dependency cache. Artifacts preserve output from a run; caches reuse rebuildable input such as downloaded dependencies.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf teaching diagram created for this course; no external artwork used.

assets.purpose: Workflow security trust boundaries concept diagram
assets.alt_text: Untrusted contribution enters read-only validation, then crosses a review boundary before an isolated protected deployment zone.
assets.caption: Workflow security trust boundaries. Keep untrusted contribution validation separate from credentialed deployment; use narrow permissions and explicit promotion.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf teaching diagram created for this course; no external artwork used.

assets.purpose: Continuous integration pipeline concept diagram
assets.alt_text: A five-stage CI flow from change event to static checks, tests, build, and required merge status checks.
assets.caption: Continuous integration pipeline. A change should pass explicit quality gates before its build output is considered eligible for promotion.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf teaching diagram created for this course; no external artwork used.

assets.purpose: Multi-environment deployment concept diagram
assets.alt_text: The same identified artifact passes through development and staging, then an approval gate, production, health checks, and rollback.
assets.caption: Multi-environment deployment. Build once, promote the same identified artifact through staged environments, and put approval before production.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf teaching diagram created for this course; no external artwork used.

assets.purpose: Choosing a reuse mechanism concept diagram
assets.alt_text: Comparison of reusable workflows, composite actions, repository scripts, templates, and their contracts.
assets.caption: Choosing a reuse mechanism. Select the abstraction based on whether teams reuse whole jobs, steps, or a repository-local script.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf teaching diagram created for this course; no external artwork used.

assets.purpose: Traceable release and provenance concept diagram
assets.alt_text: Source commit flows through build and test, recorded provenance, verification, and controlled publish or promotion.
assets.caption: Traceable release and provenance. Connect the source revision, build outputs, verification evidence, and published release.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf teaching diagram created for this course; no external artwork used.

assets.purpose: Workflow debugging decision flow concept diagram
assets.alt_text: A troubleshooting decision map for missing runs, queued jobs, failed steps, permission problems, external failures, and retesting.
assets.caption: Workflow debugging decision flow. Start with the earliest observable failure, then inspect the relevant trigger, runner, step, permission, or network.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf teaching diagram created for this course; no external artwork used.

assets.purpose: Runner infrastructure and scaling concept diagram
assets.alt_text: Runner scheduling routes jobs through a runner group and scale set to ephemeral workers, followed by cleanup and metrics.
assets.caption: Runner infrastructure and scaling. A scheduler routes jobs to eligible runners; a managed scale set can provision isolated workers and clean them up.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf teaching diagram created for this course; no external artwork used.

assets.purpose: Capstone CI/CD architecture concept diagram
assets.alt_text: Capstone architecture separates pull-request CI from verified artifacts, development, staging, protected production, and operations.
assets.caption: Capstone CI/CD architecture. Pull-request validation and release deployment use distinct trust boundaries and promote verified artifacts through environments.
assets.source_license: Original CodeLeaf teaching diagram created for this course; no external artwork used.
